title: Portable Cross-Facility Workflows for X-ray Ptychography
problem: X-ray facilities (APS, LCLS) generate orders-of-magnitude increases in data output from recent upgrades, requiring robust processing pipelines to handle data-intensive ptychography imaging with timely feedback. The increased data rates necessitate efficient computational workflows for near-real-time reconstruction at scale.
motivation: Large computing facilities can dramatically accelerate processing of data-intensive ptychography experiments, enabling faster scientific feedback and broader accessibility to advanced computing infrastructure for beamline scientists.
method: A file-based workflow architecture deployable at any ptychography beamline that orchestrates data processing across external computing facilities. Demonstrated via two experiments: processing 98 scans from Advanced Photon Source (APS) to Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF), and 15 scans from Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS) to ALCF. The system uses file-based interfaces to enable portable cross-facility data movement and distributed reconstruction.
key_novelty: Portable file-based workflow design enabling seamless cross-facility data processing where ptychography data from heterogeneous X-ray sources can be transparently reconstructed at centralized HPC facilities with standardized interfaces.
contributions: Portable software workflow framework for ptychography data processing deployable across different beamlines
Cross-facility interoperability demonstrating data exchange between APS/LCLS and ALCF computing infrastructure
File-based workflow design enabling timely feedback at high data throughput
Experimental validation at scale processing 113 total scans across multiple facilities

metrics.other: 98 scans processed from APS, 15 scans from LCLS demonstrating cross-facility capability with timely feedback

primary_theme: Cross-facility computational workflows for scientific imaging
